title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pullman, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pullman, WV
metaDescription: Pullman, Ritchie County mineral owners: legacy Big Injun sand production, 19th-century deed history, and multi-generation heir title checks.
heroLead: Pullman is a small Ritchie County community sitting within the county's broader legacy oil and gas production footprint dating back to the 1800s.
intro: Ritchie County's early oil history extends across much of the county, and Pullman's surrounding acreage carries the same pattern found throughout the area — long-producing Big Injun sand wellbores, deed records that reach back well over a century, and mineral interests split across generations of heirs.

sections.heading: Long-producing legacy wells
paragraphs: Wells around Pullman drawing from the Big Injun sand tend to be modest producers that have been on the books for decades, some under leases old enough to predate current royalty conventions entirely. If a well on your tract is still paying a flat rate, that's worth checking against West Virginia's conversion statute.

sections.heading: Tracing ownership through a century-plus of transfers
paragraphs: A Pullman-area mineral interest that started with a single 19th-century severance has typically passed through several generations of inheritance by now, often without a formal probate at each step. Establishing current ownership means working through the Ritchie County Courthouse's deed and will books in Harrisville, tract by tract.

sections.heading: Confirming a Pullman tract hasn't lapsed to unclaimed status
paragraphs: When a mineral interest goes multiple generations without a documented owner actively claiming it — royalty checks unclaimed, correspondence returned — it can eventually be reported to the West Virginia State Treasurer's unclaimed property division. Checking whether any Pullman-area family interest has reached that status is worth doing alongside a standard courthouse title search.
Recovering an interest from unclaimed property status is a separate process from establishing the underlying chain of title, but both matter before a sale can close cleanly.

faqs.question: How old are typical Pullman-area wells?
faqs.answer: Many draw from the Big Injun sand under leases that go back decades, part of Ritchie County's long legacy production history.

faqs.question: Is my old Pullman lease still paying a flat rate?
faqs.answer: Check the payment terms on your division order; flat-rate leases from this area can often be converted to a percentage royalty under state law.

faqs.question: My family's Pullman interest has never been formally divided among heirs — what now?
faqs.answer: You can typically sell your own documented share with an heirship affidavit, without waiting for a full family probate.

faqs.question: How do I check if a Pullman family interest was reported as unclaimed property?
faqs.answer: The West Virginia State Treasurer's unclaimed property division maintains searchable records separate from the courthouse deed record; both are worth checking.
